cohort: Critically ill pregnant women admitted to the Obstetric Intensive Care Unit (OICU) at the "Dr. Armando Castillo Plaza" maternity hospital in Maracaibo, Venezuela
finding: The study found that hypertensive disorders, infections, and bleeding were the leading causes of admission to the OICU, and identified risk factors for extreme maternal morbidity and mortality.
mod_finding: 62.50% of the critically ill obstetric patients underwent a segmental cesarean section.
gest_age: Preterm pregnancy (specific gestational age not mentioned)
